newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ merchandise trade trend improves in June - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ merchandise trade trend improves in June - SNZ.

text.p: Trend estimates of New Zealand exports and imports had levelled off over the last two years after rising steadily from 1992-1995, Statistics New Zealand said on Thursday.
However, in recent months the trade balance trend had improved.
Trade in June was in surplus by $150.2 million against a nine million dollar surplus a year earlier.
Unadjusted exports in the June quarter were up 4.8 percent while imports rose by 1.6 percent. The surplus was $646.5 million for the quarter, up by $188 million on the year ago quarter.
Excluding large one-offs, mainly aircraft, a surplus of $779 million would have been posted for the quarter, SNZ said.
After adjustment for seasonal effects, the trade balance for the June quarter declined to a deficit of $25 million.
This compared favourably, however, with the seasonally adjusted deficits of $390 millon for the March 1997 quarter and $199 million for the June 1996 quarter.
Exports for the year at $21.05 billion were up 2.5 percent.
Significant rises were in milk powder, butter and cheese exports. Falls were in fish, hides and wool.

Imports for the year remained virtually unchanged with falls in seven of the top 10 imports categories. Leading the falls were mechanical and electrical machinery and vehicles with fuels and paper products being the biggest rises.
